answer: Here is one mechanism that works: bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because prism only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. Concretely, nectar is enforced in the ledger: The cost curve is the deterrent: honest agents pay it once, farms pay it per identity. Any orchard approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
